name: Neptune
lede: The windiest known planet — methane-blue clouds, dark storms, and the captured moon Triton.

landmark.label: Great Dark Spot · Voyager
landmark.blurb: A large southern storm imaged by Voyager 2 in 1989; later Hubble views showed it had faded while new dark spots appeared.

missions.name: Voyager 2
missions.note: Only spacecraft visit — Great Dark Spot, rings, and Triton flyby.

researchNotes: Neptune is an ice giant like Uranus but more dynamically active. Wind speeds can exceed 2,000 km/h — among the strongest measured in the solar system.
The Great Dark Spot of 1989 was comparable in scale to Earth. Hubble later found that such storms come and go over years.
Triton orbits retrograde and shows nitrogen geysers — strong evidence it was captured from the Kuiper Belt.
folklore: Named for the Roman god of the sea. Discovery involved mathematics (Adams / Le Verrier) as much as the telescope — a triumph of celestial mechanics.
carlFocus: Cover Voyager's Great Dark Spot, extreme winds, Triton capture story, and that Neptune was predicted before it was seen.
